name: Wall Street Poker
description: Wall Street Poker is a Seven-Card Stud variant with buyable community cards. 2-7 players. 52-card deck. Deal 3 hole cards (2 down, 1 up). 4 community cards ('Wall Street') placed face-up with escalating costs (1-4 units). Players can buy a community card (goes to pot) or get a free card from deck. Named after aggressive financial bidding.

history.origins: Wall Street is a seven-card stud variant in the buy-your-card family where players pay fixed amounts to the pot to acquire cards. The name refers to the row of four face-up community cards (Wall Street) that players may buy at 1-4 units or pass for a free card from the deck. It shares mechanics with The Price is Right but offers four market cards and a free-card alternative; the theme evokes bidding and speculation in home poker.
timeline: Late 20th to early 21st century: Seven-card stud variant with buyable community cards, named after the Wall Street financial district.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck; one pack. No jokers or stripped cards.
setup.dealing: Ante. 3 hole cards (2 down, 1 up) + 4 community 'Wall Street' cards.

rules.objective: Make the best high hand and/or the best low hand from your seven cards; after declaration, the high winner and the low winner split the pot.
rules.gameplay: Wall Street: 4 community cards face-up costing 1/2/3/4 units. Each round: buy a community card (fee to pot, card replaced from deck) OR get free face-up card. Continue until 4 upcards each. Final card dealt face-down. Standard betting rounds. Best 5-card hand wins.
keyRules: Most expensive card can be wild (variant)

strategy.basic: Buy when community card strongly improves hand.
